rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an outside party (such as a customer) chooses among several configuration options, with each option being a separate choice, and the options are sent to that party before its choices are received and before work is dispatched to other teams: Model the options being sent to the outside party as a sendTask. Model each option the party chooses as its own user task, placed after that send task and before the parallel split that dispatches the work. Keep every choice as a distinct element and do not merge them into one task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an outside party (such as a customer) chooses among several configuration options, with each option being a separate choice, and the options are sent to that party before its choices are received and before work is dispatched to other teams

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description names a step with a verb and an object (for example 'send X to Y', 'deliver X to Z', 'perform a test X'), and the generated label would change that verb, use a synonym, or drop a qualifier the description states.: Label the task with the verb the description uses for that step and the object with its stated qualifiers (for example a 'test' qualifier), so the label keeps the described action and direction. Do not swap the verb for a near-synonym or a different activity type, and do not shorten the object by dropping a stated qualifier.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description names a step with a verb and an object (for example 'send X to Y', 'deliver X to Z', 'perform a test X'), and the generated label would change that verb, use a synonym, or drop a qualifier the description states.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that the options an outside party selects are each carried out by a separate team, with an example that names which team handles which option, and the work for each option must go only to the team that handles it: After the selection is received, model an exclusive gateway with one outgoing branch per option. Each branch leads to a send task addressed to the one team responsible for that option. Do not send all options to all teams, and do not use a single send task for every option.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that the options an outside party selects are each carried out by a separate team, with an example that names which team handles which option, and the work for each option must go only to the team that handles it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process sends the same information or material to several different parties, each of which carries out a different piece of work on it: Model one send task per receiving party, in the order the description gives, each labeled with what is sent and to whom. Give every party named in the description its own send task, and do not merge the dispatches into one element or leave one party out. Choose the element type from the direction of the verb: a send verb gets a send task, not a receive task or a manual task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process sends the same information or material to several different parties, each of which carries out a different piece of work on it

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process itself sends information or instructions to one or more outside parties so that they carry out work, and does not say the process waits for anything from those parties at that point: Model the step as a bpmn:sendTask, labeled with a send verb and the recipient as the description names it, placed before the outside work it triggers and connected by sequence flow. Do not model an outbound send as a bpmn:receiveTask or as a manual task, because the message direction and the task semantics would then be wrong.
